title: Journey-aligned SLI correlation + adaptive tail-sampling for analytics pipelines
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: our analytics ingest pipeline emits high-cardinality traces and logs which makes root-cause analysis expensive and slow for console backend incidents. Current SLI alerts often lack end-to-end trace context across routing, KV cache, and model‑serving hops. This ticket implements two complementary features: 1) journey‑aligned SLI correlation that stitches signals (request metrics, trace spans, sampled logs) into a single journey ID for console/analytics flows, and 2) an adaptive, low‑overhead tail-sampling layer at ingest that preserves full telemetry for anomalous or SLO-violating requests while otherwise applying budgeted sampling.
acceptance_criteria: All SLI alerts for console analytics routes include a journey_id and link to a trace or sampled log within the alert payload
Tail-sampling keeps 95% of traces relevant to SLO violations while reducing overall trace storage by at least 40% compared to current baseline
Median time-to-link from alert to trace < 5 minutes in staging and < 10 minutes in prod for detected incidents
No request path latency increase > 1.5ms p50 from adding lightweight correlation headers and sampling decision checks on the hot path
design_decisions: Use a generated journey_id propagated via x-rw-journey header across internal services rather than trying to infer from tenant+path (avoids heuristic mismatch)
Implement sampling policy as a hybrid: deterministic reservoir for high-priority tenants + adaptive tail rules based on per-route SLO deviations and anomaly scoring
Keep sampling decision fast and local: store sampling flag in the request context and attach to existing trace/span metadata to avoid extra RPCs
Persist sampled payloads to a dedicated low-latency retention tier for 7 days and tier cold storage for 90 days to balance debugability and cost
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off: deploy journey_id header propagation middleware and minimal ingest hooks to staging
2) Enable passive recording in staging for two weeks and compare coverage vs current incidents
3) Gradually enable adaptive tail-sampling in staging with conservative thresholds, run chaos traffic to validate budget behavior
4) Canary rollout to 10% of prod traffic (non-critical tenants) for 48 hours; monitor p50/p95 latency, trace storage, and incident link times
5) Full rollout with accelerated sampling thresholds once SLOs and cost targets validated; publish runbook and incident playbook update
instrumentation_changes: Add x-rw-journey header generation at console edge and middleware to propagate across async tasks
Emit a journey_id tag on every span, log line, and analytics event associated with a request
Expose per-route sampling_metrics: sample_rate, tail_events_count, ignored_due_to_budget in metrics pipeline
Add an ingest-side lightweight anomaly scorer (threshold-based with option to plug ML model later) that flips tail-sample=true for suspicious requests
dashboards: Console / Observability / Journey Coverage: % of SLI alerts with linked journey_id (goal > 90%)
Sampling Budget Dashboard: daily trace volume, tail-sample rate by route and tenant, cold vs hot storage costs
Alert-to-Trace Latency: histogram of time between SLI alert and first linked trace/log
Performance Guardrails: p50/p95 latency per route before/after header propagation and sampling checks
